# Message codes: Authors

See also: [Message codes](message-codes.md) (the index of every code) and
[Messages and codes](messages.md) (the line grammar, what a code guarantees and
when to trust one).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_message_reference.py; do not edit. -->

Trust a code only when the line is one of the lines below, a value in place of
each `<name>`, after at most one prefix: the index lists the prefixes and
`message-codes-values.md` the values.

## Codes

| Code | Level | Means | Since |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`author-ambiguous`](#author-ambiguous) | WARNING, INFO | A free-text author field (core metadata Author or Author-email, a setup.cfg or setup.py author, a dependency's author or maintainer record) was read by a guess. An address field is a list, split on ',' and ';', though one name may hold a comma ('Doe, Jane'); a name field is one author, cut only next to the complete mailboxes it holds. The INFO line is a name field read as one author though it holds ',', ';' or 'and' ('Doe, Jane' and 'Ann and Bob' cannot be told from lists). For dependencies, one line per document names the first field split and how many dependencies were. | 0.25.0 |
| [`author-invalid`](#author-invalid) | WARNING | An entry of a project's free-text author field holds an address that is no address of the form local@domain (an Author-email entry, or a mailbox in Author with '<' or '@'), or two addresses in one mailbox. The line shows the entries, the first few when several, and how many. | 0.25.0 |
| [`project-unreadable`](#project-unreadable) | WARNING | An embed with a project directory (embed-wheel --project-dir, wheel --embed with --project-dir, the library's embed_wheel_sbom) reads the project's metadata only for its declared authors, which keep their order there; the metadata could not be read: a configuration or metadata file that does not parse, is not UTF-8 or cannot be opened. The line gives what was reported. | 0.25.0 |

### `author-ambiguous`

- **Level**: WARNING, INFO.
- **Means**: A free-text author field (core metadata Author or Author-email, a
  setup.cfg or setup.py author, a dependency's author or maintainer record) was
  read by a guess. An address field is a list, split on ',' and ';', though one
  name may hold a comma ('Doe, Jane'); a name field is one author, cut only next
  to the complete mailboxes it holds. The INFO line is a name field read as one
  author though it holds ',', ';' or 'and' ('Doe, Jane' and 'Ann and Bob' cannot
  be told from lists). For dependencies, one line per document names the first
  field split and how many dependencies were.
- **SBOM effect**: weaker: what the SBOM says is less sure.
- **Pitloom did**: Recorded each entry of the split as its own author (or the
  name field as one author, for the INFO line); the SBOM is written.
- **Tell the user**: which field was split and how, as the line says. Only
  authors listed in pyproject.toml (a project directory or an sdist that has
  one) are read one by one; a wheel's METADATA, an sdist's PKG-INFO, a setup.cfg
  or setup.py author and a dependency's record are free text. They list each
  author in [project] authors of pyproject.toml and generate from the project or
  an sdist. A dependency's record is its maintainers' to fix. Do not edit the
  project's metadata for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it
  only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: AUTHOR=<authors>: split into <entry-count> next to an address; a name field is never cut between names [author-ambiguous]
  WARNING: AUTHOR_EMAIL=<authors>: split into <entry-count> on ',' or ';'; an address field cannot tell a list from one name holding a comma [author-ambiguous]
  INFO: AUTHOR=<authors>: read as one author; it may list several [author-ambiguous]
  WARNING: PACKAGE=<package> <author-key>=<authors>: split into <entry-count> next to an address; a name field is never cut between names; <dependency-count> split in all [author-ambiguous]
  WARNING: PACKAGE=<package> <author-key>=<authors>: split into <entry-count> on ',' or ';'; an address field cannot tell a list from one name holding a comma; <dependency-count> split in all [author-ambiguous]
  ```

### `author-invalid`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An entry of a project's free-text author field holds an address
  that is no address of the form local@domain (an Author-email entry, or a
  mailbox in Author with '<' or '@'), or two addresses in one mailbox. The line
  shows the entries, the first few when several, and how many.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Recorded no address for the entry; a display name stated
  before its '<' is kept as an author with no address. The SBOM is written.
- **Tell the user**: which entries hold no email address, as the line says. They
  correct the address in the project's metadata and generate again. Do not edit
  the metadata for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: AUTHOR_EMAIL=<authors>: not an email address; not recorded [author-invalid]
  WARNING: AUTHOR_EMAIL=<authors>: not an email address; <entry-count> not recorded [author-invalid]
  WARNING: AUTHOR=<authors>: not an email address; not recorded [author-invalid]
  WARNING: AUTHOR=<authors>: not an email address; <entry-count> not recorded [author-invalid]
  ```

### `project-unreadable`

- **Level**: WARNING.
- **Means**: An embed with a project directory (embed-wheel --project-dir, wheel
  --embed with --project-dir, the library's embed_wheel_sbom) reads the
  project's metadata only for its declared authors, which keep their order
  there; the metadata could not be read: a configuration or metadata file that
  does not parse, is not UTF-8 or cannot be opened. The line gives what was
  reported.
- **SBOM effect**: thinner: the SBOM says less than reading the input would.
- **Pitloom did**: Took the authors from the wheel's METADATA: authors with an
  address come first, and name-only authors joined into one Author field are
  read as one. The SBOM is embedded.
- **Tell the user**: which project directory could not be read and why, as the
  line says. They fix the project's metadata and embed again. Do not edit the
  project for them; ask first, and with nobody to ask, report it only.
- **Lines**:

  ```text
  WARNING: DIR=<dir>: project metadata not read; authors from the wheel METADATA; <failure> [project-unreadable]
  ```
